observations.corner_order: A4F0 (most rounded) > 7D2B (medium) > E916 (least rounded, sharpest). Confirmed by pixel measurement, not just eyeballing: the button's flat-left-edge is reached 5 rows down from the top edge in E916, 7 rows down in 7D2B, and 11 rows down in A4F0 - a monotonic increase in corner radius.
observations.any_other_difference: none. A pixel-diff of every pair (E916 vs 7D2B, E916 vs A4F0, 7D2B vs A4F0) produced the exact same bounding box in all three comparisons: (442,192)-(538,224), which is precisely the amber button's footprint. No pixels anywhere else in the 560x229 image differ between any pair, so corner rounding is the only difference. (I initially thought I saw a small chevron near '10:42' in one image, but the diff-bbox check proves that was a misread on my part, not a real difference - flagging that I almost reported a difference I could not actually substantiate.)
observations.content_lost: none. Header, external-share note, 宛先/差出人 fields, message body, 出所 line, and Cancel/Edit/送る controls are all present and identical in text/position across all three images.

why.visual_craft: 7D2B's medium radius reads as the most deliberate/intentional choice for a compact action button; E916 is close behind (crisp and clean, if slightly stiff); A4F0's near-pill rounding looks disproportionate for a button this small and starts to read as an accidental over-rounding rather than a considered choice.
why.coherence: The card's own outer corners are only very subtly rounded (alpha-channel check on the card's corner pixels shows the rounding resolves within ~2-3px - essentially a near-sharp rectangle, not a soft card). E916's smaller button radius sits closest to that near-sharp frame; 7D2B is a step further; A4F0's near-pill button radius diverges the most from the mostly-rectangular card it sits inside.
why.overall: 7D2B is the best balance: it is the top pick for craft and only one step behind on coherence. E916 is a solid second (best coherence, second-best craft). A4F0 is last on both axes - its rounding is the most eye-catching but the least consistent with both good button proportions and the card's own near-sharp geometry.
